abstract: We consider the quantum time complexity of the all pairs shortest paths (APSP) problem and some of its variants. The trivial classical algorithm for APSP and most all pairs path problems runs in $O(n^{3})$ time, while the trivial algorithm in the quantum setting runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, using Grover search. A major open problem in classical algorithms is to obtain a truly subcubic time algorithm for APSP, i.e. an algorithm running in $O(n^{3-\varepsilon})$ time for constant $\varepsilon>0$. To approach this problem, many truly subcubic time classical algorithms have been devised for APSP and its variants for structured inputs. Some examples of such problems are APSP in geometrically weighted graphs, graphs with small integer edge weights or a small number of weights incident to each vertex, and the all pairs earliest arrivals problem. In this paper we revisit these problems in the quantum setting and obtain the first nontrivial (i.e. $O(n^{2.5-\varepsilon})$ time) quantum algorithms for the problems.

specification.problem: Quantum time complexity of all pairs shortest paths (APSP) and variants on structured inputs (geometrically weighted graphs, small integer weights, few distinct weights per vertex, all pairs earliest arrivals): obtain quantum algorithms faster than the trivial O~(n^2.5) Grover-based bound, i.e. O(n^{2.5-epsilon}).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Complexity-level reconstruction only: problem statement and time bounds from the abstract. The abstract gives no circuits, registers, or measurement details, so the circuit plan and measurement are generic baseline assumptions, not the paper's algorithm.

registers.name: pair_index
registers.role: Assumed register indexing a source-target pair (u,v) or a candidate intermediate vertex in a Grover search

registers.name: search
registers.role: Assumed register for Grover search over candidate intermediate vertices/neighbors, queried via an adjacency/weight oracle

registers.name: work
registers.role: Assumed ancilla for oracle evaluation of weights and comparisons

specification.initial_state: Assumed uniform superposition over the search register (Hadamard on |0...0>), with graph access through a quantum adjacency-list or matrix oracle.

steps.description: For each source-target pair, prepare the uniform superposition over candidate intermediate vertices (baseline, assumed).
Apply Grover/minimum-finding with an oracle for path weights, taking about sqrt(n) iterations per pair, giving n^2 pairs times sqrt(n) = O~(n^2.5) total.
Structured-input algorithms (the paper's methods) would exploit weight structure to reduce total time to O(n^{2.5-epsilon}); details not in the abstract.

specification.measurement: Assumed baseline: measure the search register after Grover minimum-finding for each pair (u,v) to obtain the argmin intermediate vertex, repeating for success probability 1-1/poly(n). The paper's measurement procedure is not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: record the minimum path weight per pair in an n x n distance matrix, using a union bound over n^2 pairs with O(log n) repetitions, which is absorbed by the tilde in the running time.
